name: Austronesian peoples
summary: Seafaring peoples whose languages spread from Taiwan through the Philippines, Indonesia, the Pacific and as far as Madagascar, carried by outrigger canoes. (The source maps also use this name for the islands before the Austronesian expansion.)

knownFor.label: Outrigger canoe
knownFor.note: Canoes with side floats, stable enough for ocean voyages.

knownFor.label: Lapita pottery
knownFor.note: Decorated pottery of the first settlers of Remote Oceania.

knownFor.label: Star navigation
knownFor.note: Finding the way by stars, waves and birds.

location.value: Taiwan, maritime Southeast Asia, Micronesia, coastal New Guinea, Island Melanesia, Polynesia and Madagascar.

terrain.value: Islands, coasts and the open sea.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

climate.value: Tropical, with monsoon and trade winds.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

resources.value: They carried crops and animals such as rice, bananas, coconuts, breadfruit, yams, taro, pigs, chickens and dogs.

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

population.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

disease.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

migration.value: The Austronesian expansion from Taiwan (about 3000–1500 BCE), reaching Hawaiʻi by 900 CE, Madagascar in the 5th–7th centuries CE and New Zealand by 1200 CE.

economicBase.value: Wetland farming (including rice), aquaculture and sea trade.

tradeRoutes.value: Spice trade with southern India and Sri Lanka; by the end of the 1st millennium BCE, sea routes linked Han China with India, the Roman world and Africa.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible, though prestige came from canoes, shell goods and land.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

moneyAndTax.value: None in early times; exchange was by gift and barter.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

inequality.value: Varied: some societies had ranked chiefs.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

succession.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

institutions.value: Customary law (adat) and councils of elders.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

stability.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

armyAndTech.value: Spears, bows and war canoes; outrigger canoes made long voyages possible.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

territoryChange.value: Spread from Taiwan as far as Easter Island in the east, Madagascar in the west, New Zealand in the south and Hawaiʻi in the north.

alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

inventions.value: Outrigger boats, catamarans (double-hulled canoes) and the crab claw sail.

scienceEducation.value: Navigation knowledge of stars, swells and birds was passed on orally.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

openness.value: Open to new islands and contacts.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

communicationTransport.value: Seagoing catamarans and outrigger canoes, their most important innovations.

religion.value: Ancestor worship, animism and shamanism, with belief in a spirit world and powerful deities.

languageWriting.value: Austronesian languages such as Malay (Indonesian), Javanese and Tagalog; no native writing system except possibly rongorongo on Easter Island.

artsArchitecture.value: Lapita pottery (by 1200 BCE), tattooing, jade carving and rock art.

socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

sharedIdentity.value: Related languages and shared customs such as tattooing, stilt houses, jade carving and wetland farming across a huge area.

dailyLife.value: Stilt houses; foods such as rice, taro, yams, breadfruit and coconuts.

neighbours.value: Papuan and Negrito peoples, with whom they largely mixed peacefully.

ideasReligions.value: Hinduism and Buddhism (main religions in the region from the 5th to 15th centuries), then Islam and Christianity reached the islands.

colonisation.value: The first humans to reach Remote Oceania (the Northern Mariana Islands, by 1500 BCE).

riseSignals.value: Seafaring technology such as catamarans, outriggers and crab claw sails allowed rapid spread.

peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

declineSignals.value: Not a single society, so no single decline.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

outcome.value: About 386 million people speak Austronesian languages today.

sources.value: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion

overallCertainty.value: Known from linguistics, archaeology and genetics; dates are debated.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Austronesian peoples; Wikipedia: Austronesian expansion
